subject: chemistry
title: Extraction of metals by reduction with carbon
key_idea: Unreactive metals such as gold are found as the metal itself. Most metals are found as compounds in ores and must be extracted. Metals less reactive than carbon are extracted from their oxides by reduction with carbon.

blocks.text: This section covers how metals are found in the Earth's crust and why most need a chemical reaction to extract them.

items.meaning: A rock in the Earth's crust that contains a metal compound, from which the metal can be extracted.
A chemical reaction that separates a metal from its compound.

items: Unreactive metals such as **gold** are found in the Earth as the metal itself, the uncombined element.
Silver, platinum and copper can also be found as the metal itself.
Most metals are found as **compounds**, for example oxides, in ores.
Reactive metals are too reactive to exist as uncombined elements.
Extracting a metal from its compound needs a chemical reaction.
Unreactive metals such as gold are found uncombined.
Most metals are found as compounds and must be extracted by a chemical reaction.

blocks.text: This section covers how a metal oxide is reduced by heating it with carbon.

items.meaning: The loss of oxygen from a compound.
The gain of oxygen by a substance.

items: Extraction of a metal from its ore involves **reduction**: the oxide loses oxygen.
Carbon is more reactive than the metal, so carbon removes oxygen from the oxide.
Carbon displaces the metal. The carbon is oxidised, because it gains oxygen.
This works only for metals **less reactive than carbon**.

blocks.label: Word equation for iron
blocks.formula: iron oxide + carbon → iron + carbon dioxide
where: iron oxide: reduced, because it loses oxygen
carbon: oxidised, because it gains oxygen

items: In 2CuO + C → 2Cu + CO₂, copper oxide is reduced and carbon is oxidised.
In SnO₂ + C → Sn + CO₂, tin oxide is reduced. Tin is less reactive than carbon, so carbon can be used.
Heating with carbon is cheaper than electrolysis.
Heating a metal oxide with carbon removes the oxygen, so the oxide is reduced.
Carbon can only be used for metals below carbon in the reactivity series.

blocks.text: The method depends on where the metal sits compared with carbon in the reactivity series.

diagram.alt: Choose a metal to see how it is found and how it is extracted.

options.label: Copper
results: Usually an ore containing a copper compound; sometimes the metal itself

items: Metals above carbon cannot be reduced by carbon. Carbon cannot remove their oxygen.
They are extracted by electrolysis of the molten compound.
Electrolysis uses a lot of energy, so it is more expensive than heating with carbon.
Aluminium is extracted by electrolysis. Iron is extracted by heating iron oxide with carbon, which is cheaper.
Below carbon: heat the oxide with carbon.
Above carbon: electrolysis, which needs more energy and costs more.

checks.q: Explain why gold is found in the Earth as the metal itself.
checks.a: Gold is very unreactive, so it does not combine with other elements.

checks.q: Zinc oxide is heated with carbon. Which substance is reduced? Give a reason.
checks.a: Zinc oxide, because it loses oxygen.

checks.q: Why can carbon be used to extract tin from tin oxide?
checks.a: Carbon is more reactive than tin, so it removes the oxygen from tin oxide.

worked_example.question:
Nickel is extracted from nickel oxide by reduction with carbon.

Explain why carbon can be used to extract nickel from nickel oxide.
answer_points: Carbon is more reactive than nickel.
So carbon will displace (replace) nickel from nickel oxide, or carbon will remove oxygen from nickel oxide.
worked_example.tip: The converse is allowed: nickel is less reactive than carbon. The second mark follows from the first.

worked_example.question:
Most metals are extracted from ores found in the Earth's crust. The method used to extract a metal from its ore is linked to the reactivity of the metal.

Part of the reactivity series is: calcium (most reactive), aluminium, zinc, iron, copper, gold (least reactive).

Aluminium cannot be extracted by heating its oxide with carbon. Aluminium has to be extracted from its oxide by electrolysis.

Explain why.
answer_points: Aluminium is high in reactivity, or aluminium oxide is very stable.
Aluminium (oxide) cannot be reduced by carbon.
worked_example.tip: Carbon is less reactive than aluminium is allowed. Saying only that aluminium is more reactive is ignored.

worked_example.question:
Iron is a transition metal.

The reactivity series of some metals, with carbon included, is: sodium (most reactive), calcium, magnesium, carbon, zinc, iron, copper (least reactive).

Iron can be extracted from the compound iron oxide.

How is iron extracted from iron oxide? Explain your answer.

Use the information in the list.
answer_points: By reacting (heating) the iron oxide with carbon.
Because carbon is more reactive than iron, so it displaces iron.
worked_example.tip: Use only the elements in the list.
